item.title: TAN 1Q69
item.markdown:
--- page 1 ---
Tanachira Retail Corporation PCL. (TAN)
Consistent . Sustainable . Long-Term
Earnings Call Q1 2026 
15th May 2026

--- page 2 ---
Executive Summary
• Geopolitical tensions in Q1/2026 negatively affected the spending sentiment of the Group’s target customers 
• TAN can report Q1/Y2026 Revenue Growth +4.4% and delivered Net Profit (Companyy) 40.1 MB +3.2% YoY.
• Profit increased YoY: 
• Overseas operations with sales growth of 26.8% while improving cost controls
• Domestic revenue growth at 1.7%
• Tax management, primarily due to reduction in tax non-deductible items
• Foreign exchange rate revaluation gain (may positively or negatively affect financial performance in any given 
quarter)
• Domestic Blended SSSG -2.1% (No E-Tax/E-Receipt tax stimulus scheme in Q1/2026; Geopolitical tensions)
• Outstanding sales growth for Online and Beauty & Wellness Business Group
• Strong resilience against the contraction of consumer purchasing power 
• Team capability driven by a deep understanding of preserving the Brand Economic Franchise while enhancing 
competitiveness to ensure target customers continue to purchase and remain loyal to the brands
• Effective business diversification, which mitigates single-industry risk

--- page 3 ---
Revenue by Country (after Eliminating Related Party Transaction) 
• Q1/2026 Revenue Growth from China, Singapore and Vietnam
• Domestic Revenue Growth
• Revenue from Japan reduced from closed Hankyu Umeda branch.

--- page 4 ---
Business Overview Q1 2026
• Private Consumption Index: Moderate growth; Negative effects from the Geopolitical tensions and No E-Tax
• Tanachira Retail Corporation PCL. (TAN) able to report sales & profit growth. 
• Q1 2026 Revenue +4.4% YoY: Overseas strong growth, Domestic growth
• Strong Online and Beauty & Wellness performance
• Q1 2026 Domestic SSSG -2.1%: Strong Online performance, positive Beauty & Wellness, Lifestyle flat
• Q1 2026 Net Profit (Company) 40.1MB +3.2% YoY

CRM TANACHIRA CLUB Member Update
1. Membership Acquisition: As of May 10, 2026, the registered member = 84,335 members, vs 74,110 members at the end 
of Q1/2026. (New membership system officially launched on Sep. 1, 2025).
2. Member Sales Growth: +22.6% QoQ in Q1/2026, from 167MB to 205MB
3. Customer Retention: Exponential growth of +265.6%, reflecting customer retention and enhanced brand engagement
4. Purchase Frequency: Increased from 1.1 to 1.4 times (+27.3%) → improvement in active member engagement
5. Transaction Dynamics: Total number of sales transactions and the average value per transaction increased QoQ.

CRM Cross-Business Purchase
• Cross-brand purchasers made up 1.0% of total members in the initial phase.
• At 3.0% of member-driven sales, cross-brand purchase revenue shows significant room to grow.
• Cross-segment purchase data can help improve customer retention across brands.
• These findings will also guide optimization of each brand’s revenue contribution.

HARNN Revenue Development Overseas (after Eliminating Related Party Transaction)
• Overseas expansion of the HARNN brand: the Group has progressed in line with its strategic plan.
• The growth of HARNN in China has been strong, supported by a solid business foundation that is 
expected to sustain continuous long-term growth.
• Domestic revenue of HARNN also grew double-digit

--- page 11 ---
11
Revenues and Profit Snapshot (Consolidated)
Unit : MB
• Continued improvement of sales, profit and margin after COVID-19
• Q1 2026 Net Sales growth +4.4% YoY; Net Profit +3.2% YoY
• Q1 2026 GP% at 65%; maintained at expected range of 64% - 65% level 
• Seasonal Sales Performance by Quarter: Q4>Q1>Q3>Q2

--- page 12 ---
Business Group Performance
• Revenue spread across business groups → Less reliance on 
revenue from its original core brands
• Lifestyle: mainly Pandora growth (brand ambassadors, online 
channel expansion-launch of TikTok Shop, and extensive internal 
operational adjustments to better address customer demands); Cath 
Kidston lower sales from reduced branches
• Fashion: Sales growth for GANNI, United Arrows, MM6 and 
Marimekko Singapore; Lower loss from Singapore helped to improve 
overall Fashion group profit.
• Beauty & Wellness: Strong sales growth from overseas & domestic; 
Corrective measures and operational improvements contributed to 
better profit y-o-y.
• F&B: Sales dropped y-o-y due to macroeconomic conditions that 
adversely impacted consumer spending power and a decline in 
international tourist arrivals; Additional targeted marketing initiatives, 
Value-for-Money menus and communication to drive more sales

--- page 13 ---
Overseas Revenues Contribution
• International Business is growing meaningfully with increasing and dedicated resources. 
• Main objectives are (a) to start diversifying out of Thailand and (b) not solely relying on key 
brand.
• HARNN will continue to be a major contributor in all countries.
• Q1 2026 overseas contribution at 13%
• Target share of overseas revenue contribution is 17% in 2026.
Overseas Revenue Contribution to Net Sales

--- page 14 ---
Overseas Performance
• International Business is growing meaningfully as planned.
• Q1 2026 revenue from International Business Units contributed 13% to total Group Revenue.
• Q1 2026 revenue from Overseas +26.8% YoY; China sales contributed biggest portion.
• Focus on increasing sales, stop new investments in countries that are still not profitable or require further adjustments 
to their revenue-generating plans, and strictly control expenses to reduce losses

--- page 15 ---
Revenues Q1 2026
• Revenue Q1/2026 vs Q1/2025 : +4.4% YoY
By Channel: 
• Strong Online domestic & overseas performance
• High portion of Concept Stores; SIS slightly higher
• Other Offline channels: increased from revenue 
through distributors/agents in China
• Q1/2026 Domestic SSSG -2.1%; Beauty & Wellness 
and Online positive; Lifestyle flat while Fashion and 
F&B negative 
Revenue structure by Distribution Channel Revenue structure by Business Group
By Business Group:
• Beauty & Wellness: bigger contribution from 17% to 20% from 
strong domestic and overseas growth
• Lifestyle: same portion: Pandora growth (Brand Ambassador & 
Online Expansion) while Cath Kidston lower sales
• Fashion: same portion; sales growth for GANNI, United Arrows, 
MM6 & Marimekko Singapore 
• Food & Beverage: smaller portion affected by more careful 
customer spending behavior

--- page 16 ---
Gross Profit Q1 2026
• GP amount Q1 2026 increased YoY mainly from higher sales.
• GP% to Sales Q1 2026 slightly lower YoY: (still maintain at expected level)
• Control discounts to stimulate sales so the customers can more easily access the products and services of the group
• Note: Q4/2025 included One-time cost adjustments of 12.7MB; Excluding this GP of Q4/2025 would be at 63.5%
• Brand building to maintain a high level of gross profit to create long -term sustainability
• Preservation of sales guidelines that sets selling prices effectively to maintain GP% and not selling 
at unnecessary heavy discount domestically and internationally

--- page 17 ---
Selling Expense Q1 2026
• Selling Expense in Q1 2026 increased YoY mainly from
• More accumulated branches from expansion locally & abroad (rent, people, commission, fee & depreciation)
• Elevated marketing investments, particularly for the Pandora
• The change in the number of employees on a quarterly basis and the change in the number of 
branches compared by quarter remained marginal. This reflects the Group's ongoing efforts to 
control expenses.
Number of Store
Headcount: Selling

--- page 18 ---
General & Administrative Expense Q1 2026
• Q1 2026 G&A Expense improved YoY
• Reflecting ongoing expenditure controls aligned with business operations
• Lower Unrealized Loss on Exchange Rate
• Note: Q1/2025 included a one-time asset write-off of THB 0.8 million associated with the Cath Kidston Tea 
Room brand.

--- page 19 ---
Net Profit Q1 2026
• Net Profit (Company) in Q1 2026 40.1 MB +3.2% YoY
• Enhanced performance within international operations
• Effective tax management
• Exchange rate revaluation gains
• Note: Excluding 1-time accounting/audit adjustments in Q4/2025, net profit would be at approximately THB 47 million—the net profit for 
Q1/2026 contracted slightly driven by the lower revenue 
• The Group intends to build a larger business base to support future growth of the new business locally and internationally in the long term.

GovernanceSocialEnvironmental
TANACHIRA continued to operate its business under environmental principles, focusing on business growth in tandem with social development and sustainable environmental conservation.
ESG update Q1 2026
Driving sustainable product innovation and 
eco-conscious brand experiences.
✓ Introduced the “Coach of Cathay” collection with 
sustainability integrated into product design and 
development. 
✓ Utilized 30% PCR plastic packaging and 
lightweight materials to reduce virgin plastic 
consumption and waste generation. 
✓ Promoted circular consumption through reusable 
glass packaging, portable product designs, and 
sustainable retail displays across 22+ stores.
Enhancing quality of life through health-centric and 
wellness-focused lifestyle products.
✓ Curated products and services that support healthier, 
more sustainable consumer lifestyles under the 
philosophy of “Creating and Delivering Meaningful 
Lifestyle.”
✓ Launched exclusive Cath Kidston tumblers in Thailand 
and Vietnam to encourage reusable consumption habits 
and reduce single-use waste.
✓ Continued strengthening consumer well-being through 
high-quality, safe, and lifestyle-oriented product 
offerings.
Driving sustainable business growth alongside strong corporate 
governance standards.
✓ Bread Street Kitchen & Bar collaborated with Bentley Thailand to 
deliver premium lifestyle experiences and expand opportunities within 
the luxury customer segment
✓ Strengthened long-term competitiveness through enhanced brand 
reputation, customer engagement, and expansion within affluent and 
HNWI segments.
✓ Reinforced governance practices through transparent operations, 
responsible stakeholder engagement, and partnerships aligned with 
international standards.

--- page 24 ---
Outlook 2026
• The Group remains on track to achieve its 10% revenue growth target despite ongoing economic volatility, with international 
operations expected to outpace domestic business and contribute a larger proportion of total revenue.
• Domestic operations are expected to gradually recover through the expansion of distribution channels, increased online 
sales penetration, and stronger customer engagement initiatives under the TANACHIRA CLUB program, despite cautious 
consumer spending.
• Management remains focused on delivering revenue growth that exceeds expense growth through disciplined capital 
expenditure optimization, tighter control of non-essential expenses, and enhanced operational efficiency across all business 
segments. 
• In China, HARNN will discontinue its Hangzhou spa operation due to underperformance; however, the profitability of the China 
business is expected to improve significantly thereafter.
• Singapore operations are expected to demonstrate stronger performance from Q2/2026 onward, supported by the opening 
of an additional Marimekko store and the absence of significant non-recurring accounting adjustments.
• The Group continues to strengthen its long-term growth strategy through collaboration with The Saha Pathana Group, 
expansion into the value-for-money fashion segment, and ongoing Digital Transformation initiatives, including CRM and 
POS integration, real-time marketing automation, and the implementation of SAP S/4HANA ERP scheduled for Q4/2026.
